layers.core: the kernel: the DUT and its role contracts, the SDK catalogue, the host registry, the loader and the mechanisms every host has
layers.providers: adapters: each binds one external system (this host's GPIO, serial-mux, fastboot, a person) to a role
layers.frontends: views and runtime shells: the CLI and boardctrld
layers.platforms: data: shipped public hardware knowledge, one directory per vendor
layers.hooks: data: the kernel's generic hook executables

rules.why: the kernel defines the contracts; it never knows which provider fills one, and it carries no HTTP server
a provider implements a core contract against one tool; two providers share no files, only services through ctx.service()
a frontend renders commands and routes; the kernel decides what a host has

forbidden.why: the kernel is usable without a server: routes a frontend adds live under frontends/server/routes
a provider is loaded, never imported: the kernel must not know one exists
the kernel does not know how it is shown
